subject: geography
title: Coastal Management: Holderness
meta_desc: A-Level Geography AQA adventure on Holderness coastal management and Mappleton trade-offs.

concepts.def: Maintain current position with defences; Withernsea, Hornsea.
Allow sea to flood land previously defended.
Allow natural processes; most of rural Holderness.
Concrete or stone barrier; reflective designs scour beaches.
Wooden or rock barrier perpendicular to beach; traps drift.
Coastal cell strategy identifying which policy applies where.

walkthroughs.body_html: Holderness SMP: hold the line at settlements (Bridlington, Hornsea, Withernsea, Mappleton); no active intervention along rural cliffs; managed realignment at Spurn. Decisions reflect cost-benefit: defending farmland uneconomic at £2 million/km vs cost of relocating settlements.

1991: £2 million two rock groynes plus rip-rap to protect B1242 road and village (50 houses). Successful at Mappleton but caused 1.8 m/yr increased erosion at Cowden, 3 km south, losing farmland and a holiday park. Demonstrates sediment cell connectivity in management decisions.

Property owners want defences; ecologists support natural retreat; council balances limited budget. Sue Earle (Skipsea, lost home 2017) campaigned for buy-out scheme. Coastal Change Pathfinder grants provided £11 million UK-wide 2009-11 but failed to scale.
